I can't tell you how you must feel. But, I can tell you what I've learned about my own reality in my own meditation practice, and perhaps it will be relatable.

The broken pieces of me that were created in the darkest parts of my own childhood - those don't exist out there in some separate, objective reality. They aren't problems that other people can fix, even if other people planted the seeds for those problems. That isn't to say that things like therapy can't help, but rather to say - my problems with my past and my family (or rather, my problems with myself that I connect with past and family) exist purely inside me. Confronting my family wouldn't do anything for me, unless I was trying to fix my relationship with family. But, as far as my own mental health and way of life - I am an adult, responsible for myself, and the only person who can slay my demons is me. I have support from my wife and community to be the best I can be, but the one who must heal my soul is me, because the demons I've carried do not exist in anyone else. Not even in the people who originally invited them to my life.

Imo, the catharsis you must seek is with yourself. You must be the one to overcome the past, to come to terms with it, to learn from it, and let it go. Imo, what you should feel is whole, complete, and true - not because you've earned it, or because you confronted the right people, but because that is the reality of your nature and what is healthy for you to be; now you must do what you need to accept this and be aware of it.

At least, that's how life seems to me.
